claim: NixOS provides a services.mosquitto module whose default listener ACL is empty and therefore disallows all client access until ACLs are explicitly configured (e.g. acl = [ "pattern readwrite #" ] for a fully open broker).
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should be packaged as a NixOS module integrated with the canonical Mosquitto broker configuration on every jupiterOS host
quoted_support: The default ACL for a listener is empty, disallowing all accesses from all clients. To configure a completely open ACL, set acl = [ "pattern readwrite #" ] in the listener.

claim: NixOS's Mosquitto module configures per-listener users with passwords and ACLs declaratively, and can disable password-file generation via omitPasswordAuth = true (requiring either allow_anonymous or TLS client certs with use_identity_as_username).
stance_target: fleet-wide MQTT credential provisioning for ha-linux-agent can be done declaratively in NixOS config rather than imperative mosquitto_passwd commands
scope_conditions: NixOS 26.05 stable manual, Mosquitto chapter, password authentication + ACL format sections
quoted_support: Password file generation can be disabled by setting omitPasswordAuth = true for a listener; in this case it is necessary to either set settings.allow_anonymous = true to allow all logins, or to configure other authentication methods like TLS client certificates with settings.use_identity_as_username = true.

claim: The NixOS manual instructs that any added NixOS feature should have a NixOS test, and that out-of-tree projects can run full QEMU/container-based NixOS tests via pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's unreliability should be addressed with NixOS VM test infrastructure that exercises the agent end-to-end (module + service + broker) before fleet deployment
scope_conditions: NixOS 26.05 stable manual, NixOS Tests chapter; tests run QEMU VMs and/or systemd-nspawn containers defined in nodes/containers attribute sets with a Python testScript
quoted_support: When you add some feature to NixOS, you should write a test for it. NixOS tests are kept in the directory nixos/tests, and are executed (using Nix) by a testing framework that automatically starts one or more virtual machines containing the NixOS system(s) required for the test.

claim: NixOS supports testing an entire configuration in a VM before deploying it, via nixos-rebuild build-vm (plus nixos-rebuild test/boot/switch lifecycle commands and nixos-rebuild repl for inspecting config).
stance_target: jupiterOS fleet rollouts of ha-linux-agent can be pre-validated per-host in a VM instead of risking live kiosk breakage
scope_conditions: NixOS 26.05 stable manual, Changing the Configuration chapter
quoted_support: A repl, or read-eval-print loop, is also available. You can inspect your configuration and use the Nix language with# nixos-rebuild repl Finally, you can do$ nixos-rebuild build ... QEMU virtual machine that contains the desired configuration. Just do$ nixos-rebuild build-vm

claim: When writing systemd services in NixOS modules, Exec* directives require escaping (%-specifier substitution, $FOO/${FOO} expansion, whitespace splitting, ';' command splitting) using utils.escapeSystemdExecArg / utils.escapeSystemdExecArgs.
stance_target: a services.ha-linux-agent NixOS module must handle argument escaping correctly to avoid the sloppy/unreliable invocation bugs the repo currently exhibits
scope_conditions: NixOS 26.05 stable manual, Writing NixOS Modules chapter
quoted_support: By default systemd performs substitution on %<char> specifiers in these directives, expands environment variables from $FOO and ${FOO}, splits arguments on whitespace, and splits commands on ;. All of these must be escaped to avoid unexpected substitution or splitting when interpolating into an Exec* directive.
